sec: Adenoma histopathology, acral features and coarse facies

items.q: Match the pituitary tumor to its epidemiological characteristics — 1) GH adenoma 2) Prolactinoma … A) Macroadenoma; peak age 35 to 50 years; Males > Females B) Microadenoma; peak age 25 to 40 years; Females > Males
items.exp: GH adenomas are typically macroadenomas presenting at 35-50 yrs (M>F); prolactinomas are microadenomas presenting at 25-40 yrs (F>M). (Book p948)

items.q: If acromegaly or prolactinoma is diagnosed under 20 years of age, which genetic syndrome is NOT part of the MEON differential?
items.exp: Diagnosis under 20 warrants evaluation for MEN 1, McCune-Albright, and Carney complex; VHL does not cause pituitary adenomas. (Book p948)

items.q: Match the GH adenoma histopathological pattern to its clinical prognosis — 1) Sparsely granulated adenoma 2) Densely granulated adenoma … A) Bad prognosis (more aggressive, poorer response to somatostatin analogs) B) Good prognosis
items.exp: Sparsely granulated GH adenomas have a bad prognosis; densely granulated adenomas have a good prognosis. (Book p948)

items.q: What triad of pathological actions is produced by a GH-secreting macroadenoma?
opts: Hormonal excess, Stalk effect, and Mass effect
Immune suppression, Cytokine storm, and Carcinoid syndrome
Primary aldosteronism, Salt wasting, and Nephrocalcinosis
items.exp: GH macroadenomas cause hormonal excess (high GH), stalk effect (hypopituitarism/hyperprolactinemia), and mass effect (headache/visual deficits/cavernous sinus thrombosis). (Book p948)

items.q: Because epiphyseal plate fusion is complete in adults, growth hormone excess produces ___ enlargement affecting the hands and feet.
items.exp: Epiphyseal fusion is complete in adults, so growth is restricted to acral enlargement of the hands and feet. (Book p948)

items.q: A 44-year-old male notes that his shoe size and wedding ring diameter have progressively enlarged over the past five years. Internal organomegaly is present. Which visceral organ is spared from acromegalic enlargement?
items.exp: Acromegaly causes generalized visceromegaly of internal organs, but the brain is spared. (Book p948)

items.q: Which feature is NOT part of the classical coarse facies of acromegaly?
opts: Prominent supraorbital ridge and frontal bossing
items.exp: Coarse facies involves macroglossia, thickened lips/nose, prominent supraorbital ridges, frontal bossing, and prognathism; microglossia is incorrect. (Book p948)

items.q: Protrusion of the mandible resulting from excessive mandibular periosteal bone growth in acromegaly is termed:
items.exp: Protrusion of the mandible in acromegaly is called prognathism. (Book p948)

items.q: Assess the mass effects of pituitary macroadenomas: I Suprasellar extension causes chiasmatic compression with visual impairment. II Lateral expansion can compress the cavernous sinus causing thrombosis.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Mass effect causes headaches, visual deficits from chiasm compression, and cavernous sinus thrombosis from lateral extension. (Book p948)

items.q: Match the facial manifestation of acromegaly to its anatomical basis — 1) Widely spaced teeth and underbite 2) Prominent forehead bulge 3) Airway obstruction and speech change … A) Prognathism with jaw malocclusion B) Frontal bossing C) Macroglossia
items.exp: Prognathism causes malocclusion; frontal bossing creates the forehead bulge; macroglossia causes airway compromise and speech changes. (Book p948)

items.q: Histologically, GH adenomas with dense secretory granules on electron microscopy carry a ___ prognosis.
items.exp: Densely granulated GH adenomas carry a good prognosis. (Book p948)

items.q: A 40-year-old male presents with visual field loss and headaches. MRI confirms a 2.5 cm pituitary mass. His serum prolactin is mildly elevated at 45 ug/L despite lack of prolactin staining in the tumor. This finding represents:
items.exp: Large GH adenomas compress the pituitary stalk, producing stalk effect with mild hyperprolactinemia. (Book p948)
